# laravel_cloud_cache (Resource)

Manages a Laravel Cloud cache (Valkey/Redis).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravel_cloud_cache" "example" {
  name                 = "my-valkey"
  type                 = "laravel_valkey"
  region               = "us-east-2"
  size                 = "valkey-flex-250mb"
  auto_upgrade_enabled = true
  is_public            = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `auto_upgrade_enabled` (Boolean) Enable automatic upgrades.
- `is_public` (Boolean) Whether the cache is publicly accessible.
- `name` (String) Cache name (3-40 characters, lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens/underscores).
- `region` (String) Cloud region.
- `size` (String) Cache size (250mb to 500gb).
- `type` (String) Cache type (upstash_redis, laravel_valkey).

### Optional

- `eviction_policy` (String) Eviction policy (Valkey only, defaults to allkeys-lru).

### Read-Only

- `connection_details` (Attributes) Read-only connection details for the cache. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--connection_details))
- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `status` (String) Cache status.

<a id="nestedatt--connection_details"></a>
### Nested Schema for `connection_details`

Read-Only:

- `hostname` (String)
- `password` (String, Sensitive)
- `port` (Number)
- `protocol` (String)
- `username` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import laravel_cloud_cache.example "{cache_id}"
```
